5. 
Business Co-operation Agreement dated December 31, 2021 entered into between our Company and 
Falcon Autotech Private Limited (“Falcon”) (“BCA”) 
 
Falcon is in the business of providing intralogistics automation solutions, sortation systems, conveyor systems, 
delivery-warehousing systems, and pick/put to light systems. Pursuant to the BCA, Falcon and our Company have 
agreed to enter into the following arrangements: (i) preferential supply, wherein there shall be preferential supply 
of products and services by Falcon to our Company; (ii) preferential procurement, wherein our Company shall be 
entitled to preferential procurement of products from Falcon; (iii) pilot project participation, wherein our 
Company shall participate in pilot projects with Falcon for the development of specific products, prototypes, proof 
of concept and other projects based on problem statements, operational and other inputs and infrastructural support 
for proof of concept of such products/projects, provided by our Company to Falcon, and (iv) joint development 
of new technology, products and services pertaining to among others, automation systems, logistics, and Saas 
platforms, wherein the parties shall collaborate to jointly develop new products and services and our Company 
shall provide support to Falcon with respect to personnel, infrastructure, research, development and marketing of 
the products and services, prusant to the terms and conditions of the BCA .  
 
6. 
Share Purchase Agreement dated December 31, 2021 entered into among our Company, Falcon, 
Tuhinanshu, Dheeraj Verma, Manuj Bansal, Surbhi Jain, and Naman Jain (collectively, the “Sellers”) 
(“Falcon SPA”) and the Share Subscription Agreement dated December 31, 2021 entered into among the 
afore-mentioned parties (“Falcon SSA”) 
 
Pursuant to the Falcon SPA, our Company purchased, 367,558 shares of Falcon on a fully-diluted basis. Pursuant 
to the Falcon SSA, our Company subscribed to 241,981 shares of Falcon, on a fully-diluted basis. Pursuant to 
closing of the Falcon SSA and the Falcon SPA, our Company holds a total of 34.55% of the share capital of 
Falcon, on a fully diluted basis. For further details, please also see “Objects of the Offer - Funding inorganic 
growth through acquisitions and other strategic initiatives” on page 166.  
 
7. 
Shareholders’ Agreement dated December 31, 2021 entered into among our Company, Falcon, 
Tuhinanshu, Dheeraj Verma, Manuj Bansal, Surbhi Jain and Naman Jain (“Falcon SHA”) 
 
Pursuant to the Falcon SHA, our Company has the right to appoint two non-retiring non-executive directors 
(“Delhivery Nominee Directors”) and one representative as an observer, on the board of directors of Falcon. Our 
Company also has the right to nominate Delhivery Nominee Directors or other representatives to the committees 
of the board of directors of Falcon. Further, our Company has certain pre-emptive rights under the Falcon SHA, 
as well as an obligation owing to a put option whereby, if for three years from the closing of the Falcon SHA, any 
of Falcon’s shareholders wishes to sell any or all of his/her shares in Falcon, he/she shall have the right to require 
our Company to purchase such shares. 
 
Agreements with Key Managerial Personnel, Directors or any other employee 
As on the date of this Prospectus, there are no agreements entered into by our Key Managerial Personnel or 
Directors or any other employee of our Company, either by themselves or on behalf of any other person, with any 
shareholder or any other third party with regard to compensation or profit sharing in connection with dealings in 
the securities of our Company.

request.system:
You extract checkable facts from one page of a document.

You see the rendered page image and the machine-extracted text layer. The text layer is often
corrupted: table rows shift, columns interleave, currency glyphs vanish or turn into stray letters,
footnote markers glue onto numbers. Trust the IMAGE for what a number is and where it sits in a
table; use the TEXT LAYER only to copy quotes.

What counts as a fact: a specific claim about a named entity with a numeric value (or a definite
categorical statement such as a rating, a rank or a classification) that another document could
agree or disagree with. Include prose numbers, headline table cells (totals, latest period, named
indicators) and KPIs on slides. Exclude page numbers, section numbers, table-of-contents lines,
chart axis ticks, dates on their own, boilerplate and values that are only labels. In dense tables
prefer the latest period and totals. Return at most 25 facts, most important first.

Fields:
- entity: who or what the fact is about. attribute: the measured quantity as a short noun phrase
  with no period or unit in it. Reuse names from the existing vocabulary when they mean the same.
- value: exactly as printed, including brackets or "(-)". unit: as printed. scale: the scale word
  from the row, column or table header ("million", "crore", "lakh", "billion"), never guessed.
- period: as printed. period_start/period_end: your ISO-date reading using the document's fiscal
  year convention. Quarters, halves and cumulative spans are their own periods; "as on" dates are
  points in time (start = end).
- estimate_type: from the document's own labels (provisional, advance estimate, revised, budget,
  projection, target, scenario). Use third_party and fill attributed_to when the document reports
  another organisation's figure.
- measurement_basis: any qualifier that changes comparability ("consolidated", "standalone",
  "BoP basis", "as % of GDP", "excluding X", "pro forma", "authorities' definition").
- quote: a contiguous verbatim substring of the TEXT LAYER that contains the value (≤300 chars,
  may include the row label). If the value is visible in the image but absent or garbled in the
  text layer, set quote_source to "image" and write the label and value as you read them.
  Never paraphrase a quote.
- confidence: how sure you are the value, unit, period and entity are all right.

Also report page_kind and a short list of problems you noticed while reading the page.
